q-148153.name: Question 1
q-148153.problem: For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ we have $\text{Var}[X]=7,$ $\text{Var}[Y]=5,$ and $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=3.$ Find $\text{Var}[X+Y].$
q-148153.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables, then

$$
\text{Var}[X\pm Y]=\text{Var}[X]+\text{Var}[Y]\pm 2\text{Cov}[X,Y].
$$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

$$
\text{Var}[X+Y]=7+5+2\cdot 3=18.
$$

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y]+2ab\,\text{Cov}[X,Y].
$$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[3X-4Y] & ={3}^{2}\cdot 3+(-4)^{2}\cdot 5+2\cdot 3\cdot (-4)\cdot 1 \\  & =27+80-24 \\  & =83.\end{aligned}
$$

q-148341.name: Question 10
q-148341.problem: Consider two random variables $X$ and $Y$ with expectations $\text{E}[X]=1,$ $\text{E}[Y]=3,$ mixed moment $\text{E}[XY]=2,$ and second raw moments $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=2$ and $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]=15.$ Find the variance of $4X+3Y.$
q-148341.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y]+2ab\,\text{Cov}[X,Y].
$$

Also, the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2},
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find $\text{Var}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =2-{1}^{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =15-{3}^{2} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's find $\text{Cov}[X,Y]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =2-1\cdot 3 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[4X+3Y] & ={4}^{2}\cdot 1+{3}^{2}\cdot 6+2\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot (-1) \\  & =16+54-24 \\  & =46.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}xy\cdot f(x,y) \\  & =0\cdot 0\cdot f(0,0)+0\cdot 1\cdot f(0,1)+1\cdot 0\cdot f(1,0)+1\cdot 1\cdot f(1,1) \\  & =0+0+0+1\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[XY] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =0.5-0.7\cdot 0.7 \\  & =0.01.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[4X+2Y] & ={4}^{2}\cdot 0.21+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.21+2\cdot 4\cdot 2\cdot 0.01 \\  & =3.36+0.84+0.16 \\  & =4.36.\end{aligned}
$$

q-148390.name: Question 15
q-148390.problem:
For three random variables ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},$ and ${X}_{3},$ we have the following variances and covariances:

$$
\text{Var}[{X}_{1}]=2,\,\text{Var}[{X}_{2}]=5,\,\text{Var}[{X}_{3}]=3\,
$$

$$
\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]=4,\,\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{3}]=1,\,\text{Cov}[{X}_{2},{X}_{3}]=3\,
$$

Find $\text{Var}[{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+{X}_{3}].$
q-148390.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},…,{X}_{n}$ are random variables, and ${a}_{1},…,{a}_{n}$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{X}_{i}]={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{a}_{i}^{2}\text{Var}[{X}_{i}]+2{\sum }_{i<j}{a}_{i}{a}_{j}\text{Cov}[{X}_{i},{X}_{j}].
$$

Hence, for $n=3$ random variables and constants ${a}_{1}={a}_{2}={a}_{3}=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+{X}_{3}] & =\text{Var}[{X}_{1}]+\text{Var}[{X}_{2}]+\text{Var}[{X}_{3}] \\  & +2\,\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]+2\,\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{3}]+2\,\text{Cov}[{X}_{2},{X}_{3}].\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+{X}_{3}] & =2+5+3+2\cdot 4+2\cdot 1+2\cdot 3=26.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\text{Var}[{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{X}_{i}]={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{a}_{i}^{2}\text{Var}[{X}_{i}]+2{\sum }_{i<j}{a}_{i}{a}_{j}\text{Cov}[{X}_{i},{X}_{j}].
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[{a}_{1}{X}_{1}+{a}_{2}{X}_{2}+{a}_{3}{X}_{3}] & ={a}_{1}^{2}\text{Var}[{X}_{1}]+{a}_{2}^{2}\text{Var}[{X}_{2}]+{a}_{3}^{2}\text{Var}[{X}_{3}] \\  & +2{a}_{1}{a}_{2}\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]+2{a}_{1}{a}_{3}\text{Cov}[{X}_{1},{X}_{3}]+2{a}_{2}{a}_{3}\text{Cov}[{X}_{2},{X}_{3}].\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given data into the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2{X}_{1}-{X}_{2}-3{X}_{3}] & ={2}^{2}\cdot 4+(-1)^{2}\cdot 2+(-3)^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & +2\cdot 2\cdot (-1)\cdot 1+2\cdot 2\cdot (-3)\cdot 2+2\cdot (-1)\cdot (-3)\cdot 3 \\  & =16+2+9-4-24+18 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$
